hub.speaker: The Tallyman
hub.text: Mill's yours to walk. Mind the wheel pit. Two men have gone down it since spring, and one of them was me.

text_variants.text: Eleven bushels and a name I'm not saying out loud in my own mill. You'll keep it the same way, if you please.

tally_walk.speaker: The Tallyman
tally_walk.text: Right. Barley in, barley out, household by household. Every column adds but one. That one's been short three seasons running, and it's getting shorter.

options.text: Could be the count's off and the crop's fine.

tally_count.speaker: The Tallyman
tally_count.text: Four counts, and the last one with the headman's own stick alongside mine. The stick came out the same as my tally, all the way down the column. If the count were wrong, the stick would have caught it. So it's the crop.

tally_name.speaker: The Tallyman
tally_name.text: Not saying it aloud. But their entries are honest to the grain, and that's how you know. A thief rounds up. They round down and carry the shame home with them.

options.text: Their crop failed, and they let the village think worse.

tally_truth.speaker: The Tallyman
tally_truth.text: Three seasons of it. Tell the headman gently or don't tell him at all. He's a fair man on a good day. He has not had one lately.
